title: Four Knights Game: the ideas
line: Both sides bring out both knights first: a calm, sound start.

steps.text: In the Four Knights Game both sides bring out both knights before anything else. Knights guard the center.
Push the pawn in front of your king two squares. It takes space in the center and frees your queen and a bishop.

also.d2d4: Pushing the queen's pawn is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson pushes the king's pawn.

steps.text: Bring the knight out to attack Black's pawn on e5.

also.b1c3: That is the Vienna Game, also sound. This lesson brings this knight out first.
also.f1c4: That is the Bishop's Opening, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out. It guards your pawn on e4.

also.f1c4: That is the Italian Game, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out.
also.f1b5: That is the Ruy Lopez, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out.
also.d2d4: That is the Scotch Game, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out.

steps.after: This is the Four Knights Game. The position is the same on both sides.

steps.text: Here both sides go on copying: bishops out, castling, a pawn to guard the center.
Bring your other bishop out to pin the knight on f6 to the queen.
steps.after: Black copies again, a slip often made at club level; masters take your knight on c3. You are a move ahead, so you strike first.

steps.text: Take the knight that guards Black's king, before Black can do the same to you.

also.c3d5: That is also sound. This lesson takes the knight.

steps.after: If the queen took back, your knight would jump to d5 and attack it. So a pawn takes, and the king loses its pawn cover.

summary: Four knights out guard the center. When the position is the same on both sides, the side to move strikes first.
